_readme: Pi Auto Model routing for this workspace's two local servers. First matching rule wins;
rules are evaluated before scenarios, so scenarios are intentionally absent - a rule
catch-all already covers every request and dead config is worse than none.
Target IDs match against provider/model OR the bare model id (candidate-resolver
matchesTarget), which is why the short forms below work. Validate with
/auto-model models, /auto-model rules and /auto-model doctor.
Thresholds come from measuring this package's own analyzer (src/task/local-analyzer.ts),
not from guessing. Measured complexity for short prompts:
explain what this reducer does .... 0.108 [explain]
rename a variable ................. 0.111 [mixed]
change a button label ............. 0.111 [code-edit]
refactor the auth module .......... 0.117 [refactor]
modal shows a stale closure ....... 0.120 [mixed]   <- invisible to complexity
fix the typo in the README ........ 0.318 [debug]   <- looks like real debugging
fix the race condition ............ 0.323 [debug]
debug this error / root cause ..... 0.408 [debug]
design + tradeoff + plan steps .... 0.618 [plan,architecture]
The analyzer is keyword driven (fix|bug|error|exception|stack trace -> debug) so score
alone ranks 'fix the typo' next to 'debug this error', and misses genuine hard work that
never says those words. Hence promptMatches rules first, score only as a backstop.

rules.name: trivial-edit-to-light
rules._why: Before the debug rules: 'fix the typo' scores 0.318 and is tagged debug, which would otherwise escalate a one-word edit to the large model.

rules.name: deep-work-to-heavy
rules._why: The signals that actually predict hard work but are invisible to the keyword analyzer: concurrency, invariants, migrations, trust boundaries, nondeterminism.

when.promptMatches: race condition|dead ?lock|stale closure|concurren|async race|root cause|diagnose|invariant|state machine|schema|migrat|encrypt|token|session|offline queue|dedup|idempot|backpressure|flaky|intermittent|nondetermin|memory leak|dead code|architect|redesign|trade-?offs?|why (does|is|doesn't|doesn t)|not working|doesn't work

rules.name: reasoning-kinds-to-heavy
rules._why: Kinds the analyzer does detect reliably, when they imply reasoning rather than production of text.

rules.name: high-complexity-to-heavy
rules._why: Backstop only. Measured 'debug this error' reaches 0.408 and design+tradeoff 0.618, so 0.35 catches real debugging without promoting routine edits (all <= 0.12).

rules.name: production-kinds-to-light
rules._why: Drafting text, tests and scoped edits: the small model is adequate and much faster.

rules.name: default-to-light
rules._why: Catch-all: escalate on evidence, never by default. maxComplexity 1 always matches because the analyzer clamps to [0,1].
